issue.title: Fix Host based routing to check path

issue.body: - [x] Initially raised as discussion #2243 - Python version: `3.10` - Starlette version: `starlette==0.31.0` --- Since there has not been any response in the discussion for over two weeks and I have been debugging this for quite some time I am opening an issue on this. When registering `Host()` routes with the same subdomain, only the first object is registered in the application. For the example below, only the Foo Routes will respond 200 OK, but the Bar Routes will return a 404: ```python Host("api.example.com", name="Foo Routes", app=Router(routes=[ # 200 OK Mount("/foo", name="Foo Mount", routes=[ Route("/foo", foo, name="Foo") ]), ])), Host("api.example.com", name="Bar Routes", app=Router(routes=[ # 404 Not Found Mount("/bar", name="Bar Mount", routes=[ Route("/bar", bar, name="Bar") ]), ])), ``` If you comment out the `Host()` objects and only use `Mount()` objects like this, you can see that having multiple `Mount()` objects with the same path works fine, and both Foo and Bar routes return 200 OK: ```python Mount("/foo", name="Foo Mount", routes=[ # 200 OK Route("/foo", foo, name="Foo") ]), Mount("/bar", name="Bar Mount", routes=[ # 200 OK Route("/bar", bar, name="Bar") ]), ``` I have recently moved to Starlette from Sanic (a different framework where you are able to do this (see code example/comparison in https://github.com/encode/starlette/discussions/2243#discussioncomment-6768255) which is the reason I discovered the issue. Here is a full snippet that demonstrates the problem: ```python # example.py from starlette.applications import Starlette from starlette.routing import Host, Mount, Route, Router from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse import uvicorn async def home(request): return PlainTextResponse("home\n") async def foo(request): return PlainTextResponse("foo\n") async def bar(request): return PlainTextResponse("bar\n") ROUTES = [ Route("/", endpoint=home), Host("api.example.com", name="Foo Routes", app=Router(routes=[ # 200 OK Mount("/foo", name="Foo Mount", routes=[ Route("/foo", foo, name="Foo") ]), ])), Host("api.example.com", name="Bar Routes", app=Router(routes=[ # 404 Not Found Mount("/bar", name="Bar Mount", routes=[ Route("/bar", bar, name="Bar") ]), ])), ] for r in ROUTES: print(r) # Notice the print, it seems like both Host() objects are registered to the # speicified subdomain, but accessing the routes only works for the Foo Routes... print("----") app = Starlette(routes=ROUTES) if __name__ == '__main__': uvicorn.run("example:app", host='0.0.0.0', port=8000, reload=True) # Run tests: # curl -i api.example.com:8000/foo/foo # 200 OK # curl -i api.example.com:8000/bar/bar # 404 Not found ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > - We're using [Polar.sh](https://polar.sh/encode) so you can upvote and help fund this issue. > - We receive the funding once the issue is completed & confirmed by you. > - Thank you in advance for helping prioritize & fund our backlog.
